scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation at Walmart. Let me start by going through what happened step by step. First, I've been working at Walmart for about a month now, mainly in the inventory area in the backroom. My job involves handling inventory, and sometimes we have to lift heavy boxes as part of our regular duties. I don't usually interact much with customers since I'm mostly in the backroom. One of my coworkers is a woman in her early to mid-30s. She seems physically fit and doesn't have any obvious disabilities that I can tell. Let's call her Fcw for short. So, Fcw approached me and asked if I could help her lift a heavy box. I said, "Of course," and walked over to the box with her, expecting us to do a team lift. But when we got to the box, she just stood there watching me. I asked, "Are you ready?" and she said, "Yes, it just needs to go in that bin," pointing to a metal shelving unit about four feet high. I said, "Okay, let's do it," and she responded, "It's too heavy for me. Can you please lift it into the bin?" I replied, "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me." Fcw then said, "If you're not willing to help me, I'll find someone who will," and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team, who's not my boss but the most senior person directing us, walked up to me and said, "I just spoke to Fcw, and the next time someone asks for help, you need to help them. That's part of being a team." I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying, "We're both paid to do the exact same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, then she shouldn't have taken the job. I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team, and if you would like to discuss this further, we can do it with HR present." At this point, I felt pretty annoyed and stormed off too. Now, I'm wondering if I was the asshole in this situation because it seems like it's two against one. Let me think about this. First, I need to consider the expectations of the job. We're both paid to do the same job, which includes lifting heavy boxes. So, if Fcw can't perform the tasks, maybe she shouldn't have taken the job. But she seems physically fit, so perhaps she's just trying to get me to do her work for her. On the other hand, asking for help is part of being a team. If someone is struggling with a task, it's reasonable to ask for assistance. But in this case, Fcw didn't seem to be struggling; she just wanted me to do the entire lift while she watched. That seems unfair. I also need to think about the response from the head guy. He told me that helping others is part of being a team, but I clarified the situation, explaining that I wasn't willing to do all the heavy lifting for her. I also mentioned that if she can't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job. That might have come off as confrontational, especially since I stormed off afterward. I wonder if there's a middle ground here. Maybe I could have helped her with the lift but also communicated that I expect her to contribute as well. That way, we're both doing our part, and it's fair. Also, considering the workplace dynamics, it's important to maintain a good relationship with coworkers and team leaders. Storming off might have made things worse, especially if it's perceived as being uncooperative. In summary, while I understand the frustration of being asked to do someone else's work, there might have been a better way to handle the situation by setting boundaries without being confrontational. Maybe discussing the issue with HR or finding a compromise with Fcw could have been a more constructive approach.
